newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho troops move in to flush out rebel police.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho troops move in to flush out rebel police.

text.p: Heavy gunfire erupted in Lesotho's capital Maseru on Sunday as army troops loyal to Prime Minister Ntsu Mokhehle's government moved in to quell mutinous policemen, witnesses said.

Witnesses said two armoured cars were speeding around the front of the police headquarters and firing at the building with mounted machineguns amidst bursts of shouts over a loudhailer calling on the rebels to give themselves up.
A Reuters correspondent on the scene said heavy-calibre machineguns, automatic rifles and hand grenades were used and that intermittent heavy gunfire was heard in Maseru over the past hour.

The 11-day-old police mutiny began when eight officers seized control of the police headquarters in the southern African mountain kingdom surrounded by and reliant on South Africa. The mutiny has led to a national police strike since the rebels called on officers to support their cause on Thursday.
"The army has surrounded the (police) headquarters and charge office this morning. It looks as though the army was not attacking but somebody sparked the shooting," a Western diplomat told Reuters.
"The shooting is centred around the charge office and not the headquarters," he said.
A barrage of very heavy gunfire started at 6.30 a.m. (0430 GMT) and was sustained for about a quarter of an hour.
Sirens sounded in the city for about 10 minutes shortly after the shooting started.

The eight mutinous officers are resisting arrest for the alleged killing of three fellow officers in 1995. Up to 60 other policemen had joined them in occupying the police headquarters since their siege began.
Early on Sunday, soldiers from the Lesotho Defence Force took up positions at the main entrance to the capital and were blocking traffic from entering the city centre.
"The army is intervening at the police headquarters," an army lieutenant manning a roadblock leading into Maseru, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
Maseru's streets were deserted as army vehicles and armoured personnel carriers drove through the capital.
